disease_label_per_paper: TNF receptor-associated periodic fever syndrome in end-stage renal failure due to secondary amyloidosis
presentation_summary: Forty-four-year-old man was referred to nephrology for uncontrolled hypertension and renal failure, with leg edema extending to the lower thighs, fatigue, and headaches.
He had prior workup showing hemoglobin 12 g/dL, creatinine 1.9 mg/dL, BUN 66 mg/dL, and proteinuria 4.0 g/24h; at hospitalization 24-hour proteinuria was 7.36 g and creatinine was 2.5 mg/dL.

Blood pressure at outpatient presentation was 195/110 mmHg. He was hospitalized with nephrotic syndrome; kidney function worsened during hospitalization, later reaching creatinine 6.3 mg/dL before biopsy.
After biopsy revealed AA amyloidosis, history clarified recurrent febrile periods since age 9 lasting approximately 1 week to 10 days, unpredictable and not responsive to ibuprofen or paracetamol.

Febrile periods were often accompanied by headaches or focal migratory myalgia. His two male children had similar recurrent fevers since about age 3, usually lasting two weeks and accompanied by abdominal pain and migratory arthritis.
Kidney biopsy, TNFRSF1A mutation confirmation, anakinra response, dialysis, transplant, and final diagnosis are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking context.
